newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen down in sympathy with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen down in sympathy with JGBs.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen futures contract ended easier on Wednesday in sympathy with the Japanese government bond market which was knocked down by a local news agency report quoting a politician as saying a large supplementary budget must be considered, traders said.
Jiji news agency quoted Taku Yamazaki, a senior member of the Liberal Democratic Party, as saying that a supplementary budget worth about five trillion yen must be considered.

Yamazaki said in an election campaign speech that an extra budget containing 3.5 trillion yen worth of public works projects must be considered at a special parliamentary session after general elections on October 20.
Interest swap rates (IRS) were pushed up in line with the JGB market tumble, negatively affecting the Euroyen prices.
March ended at the day's low of 99.12, after opening at 99.14 and rising to a high of 99.17.
One-year IRS was quoted at 0.67/0.71 percent, up from Tuesday's 0.65/69. Two-year IRS was quoted at 1.04/1.08 percent, compared with Tuesday's 1.00/1.04 percent.
